tagline: The Streamer Awards named its Best VTuber shortlist and the internet had opinions. hololive Meet landed a Stockholm slot. Phase Saga turned one and Filian stayed DEBUT DELAYED. Week 22, and counting.
inThisIssue: Streamer Awards 2026 Best VTuber: TheBurntPeanut nominated alongside Ironmouse, Koseki Bijou, Crelly, and Gigi Murin — he won in 2025 and the community is debating whether that should happen twice; voting closes October 31
hololive Meet makes its European debut at DreamHack Stockholm November 27-29 — Mori Calliope, Nerissa Ravencroft, and Elizabeth Rose Bloodflame on stage; Shattered Legends panel on site

lead.title: Streamer Awards 2026 Best VTuber: TheBurntPeanut is back on the shortlist after winning in 2025, nominated alongside Ironmouse, Koseki Bijou, Crelly, and Gigi Murin — ceremony November 12 in Los Angeles, voting closes October 31
lead.body: The Streamer Awards 2026 announced its nominees on October 16. The Best VTuber category lists five names: TheBurntPeanut, Ironmouse, Koseki Bijou, Crelly, and Gigi Murin. TheBurntPeanut won the same category last year, ending Ironmouse's three-year winning streak, and the return nomination landed with the same community response the win generated — immediate debate over whether a creator who has historically called himself a PTuber, not a VTuber, belongs in the category at all. On his October 17-18 stream he responded to the criticism by revealing a joke redesign of his peanut avatar: long orange hair and a promised BBL, presented as good-faith compliance with the critics. The joke landed differently across different parts of the community. Supporters point to his popularity as the only metric that matters for a viewer-voted award; critics point to prior public statements distancing himself from VTubing, to the opera background Ironmouse brings to her work, and to Koseki Bijou, Crelly, and Gigi Murin as nominees who are VTubers in every conventional sense. Ironmouse said she was cringing at all the people who were mad at TheBurntPeanut. The other nominees have not publicly commented. The Streamer Awards ceremony is November 12 in Los Angeles, red carpet at 2:30 PM PT and main show at 5:30 PM PT. Voting is live at the Streamer Awards official site through October 31. TheBurntPeanut won in 2025. The community has been arguing about it since. The argument has not resolved. It has thirteen more days until October 31 to not resolve.

stories.title: hololive Meet announces European debut at DreamHack Stockholm — November 27-29 at Stockholmsmässan; Calliope, Nerissa, Elizabeth Rose Bloodflame performing; Shattered Legends panel on site
stories.blurb: COVER Corporation announced on October 19 that hololive Meet will make its European debut at DreamHack Stockholm 2026, running November 27-29 at Stockholmsmässan. The main event is a SUPER KARAOKE PARTY on November 28 at 13:00 CET in Victoriahallen, featuring Mori Calliope, Nerissa Ravencroft, and Elizabeth Rose Bloodflame. The event also includes meet-and-greet application windows across November 27-28, a booth with video messages from Tsunomaki Watame, Airani Iofifteen, Gigi Murin, and Rindo Chihaya, and a dedicated Shattered Legends panel with Nerissa Ravencroft and Mori Calliope — their second announced joint appearance in November after the actual play series itself. The Stockholm appearance marks hololive Meet's fifth year of events and its first stop in the Nordic region. COVER notes the talent lineup may change at short notice; ticketing details at dreamhack.com/stockholm/hololive/.

stories.title: NIJISANJI Extreme Match Overwatch: Team Wanope wins — Ratna Petit and Lauren Iroas organized the four-team event; final broadcast on NIJISANJI's official YouTube at 15:00 JST October 25
stories.blurb: NIJISANJI Extreme Match Overwatch ran its main tournament on October 25 at 15:00 JST on NIJISANJI's official YouTube channel, with Team Wanope taking the championship. Four teams competed in a round-robin format followed by a final and third-place match: Wanope, TEAM 01, Hacks Eye 1/4, and D4P4 were the field. Ratna Petit and Lauren Iroas organized; Aosiru provided commentary. Blizzard supplied participant team skins. The event ran simultaneously with the Phase Saga one-year anniversary, making October 25 the highest simultaneous viewer-demand day in VTuber content since the Yokohama K-Arena triple-header. The Extreme Match Overwatch is the second in the series following the VALORANT edition earlier in 2026. Full results and VODs at the NIJISANJI YouTube channel; bracket details at wikiwiki.jp.

stories.title: NIJISANJI and NIJISANJI EN Haunted School Halloween merchandise on sale October 20 — eight livers, nine product types, limited quantities
stories.blurb: NIJISANJI and NIJISANJI EN launched Haunted School Halloween merchandise on October 20 at 18:00 JST through the official stores in Japan and overseas. Eight livers are featured: Ars Almal, Sakaki Nesu, Shiina Yuika, Sister Claire, Nagisa Trout, Hitotsubashi Ayato, Machida Chima, and Julio Dorr. Products include acrylic stands at 1,900 yen, random photo-style cards at 350 yen, can badge sets at 1,500 yen, and costumes at 2,500 yen each, with per-checkout purchase limits applied. Two illustrators produced the full-body Halloween-themed visuals. The collection follows the Secret Favor Voice pack released October 6, extending NIJISANJI's Q4 merchandise calendar through October alongside the Extreme Match Overwatch on the event side.

stories.title: Phase Saga reaches one year with five members — Welcome to Sagaville anniversary stream October 25; anniversary merch live; Phase Connect silent on Filian; @Filian_VT1 enters DEBUT DELAYED Week 22
stories.blurb: October 25 marked one year since Phase Connect's Phase Saga generation debuted. Five members held the Welcome to Sagaville anniversary stream: Bibi Biscuit, Wilhelmina Frost, Malice Evermore, Nitya Nil, and Sinon Sinfonia. The Phase SAGA First Anniversary merchandise collection launched on the official shop, including an embroidered hoodie, keychains, a plush, and a standee. Phase Connect posted nothing about @Filian_VT1 around the anniversary. The community's third pre-debut behavioral indicator — the approximately eleven-day account quiet period that the tracker had been watching since October 13 — did not produce a debut announcement. @Filian_VT1 enters Week 22 of DEBUT DELAYED. The October 24-25 resolution window the prediction thread described as having perfect narrative geometry passed without a Phase Connect post. The merch dropped. The debut did not.

stories.title: Hoshimachi Suisei plays GLION Arena Kobe October 21 — Once Upon a Stellar tour is two cities down, Aichi November 7 and Fukuoka November 12 remain
stories.blurb: Hoshimachi Suisei played the Kobe leg of her Once Upon a Stellar arena tour at GLION Arena Kobe on October 21 at 19:00 JST, the third stop of the four-city run under her Studio STELLAR independent agency label. The show streamed digitally with archive access available until November 20 at 23:59 JST at 7,000 yen through SPWN. Recording was permitted for specific songs. Two stops remain: Dolphins Arena in Nagoya on November 7 and Marine Messe Fukuoka on November 12. The tour opened at Yokohama Arena on September 8-9 and is finishing the year on its original announced schedule. Kobe is done.

indieSubhead: NO AGENCY, NO PROBLEM — NEWS FROM THE SELF-MADE CORNER OF THE SCENE

indies.title: Namirisu debuts today, October 26 — independent VTuber closes the active October Q4 debut class; CapoCoda follows October 29
indies.blurb: Namirisu debuts today as the latest independent VTuber in the October Q4 launch cohort. CapoCoda is scheduled for October 29, closing out the class that opened with Ome Teoru on October 10 and Nibbelle on October 11. The cohort launched into the densest agency event week of the year — NIJISANJI Extreme Match, Phase Saga anniversary, and the DreamHack Stockholm announcement all landed in the same seven-day window. The post-event discovery window, historically above-baseline for indie first-stream retention, opens as October's agency calendar clears into November. CapoCoda on the 29th is the last scheduled indie debut before the November slate. Debut tracking at hololist.net.

tea.text: The /vt/ TheBurntPeanut nomination thread cycled through three stages in 48 hours. Stage one: whether he belongs in the category. Stage two: whether the category's definition should be set by the community or the awards organizers. Stage three, which arrived at post 400: whether any of this debate would exist if he had not won last year. The consensus is no. Ironmouse said she was cringing, which the thread read as permission to post her cringe compilation a fourth consecutive time this month. The joke redesign — long orange hair and a promised BBL — has been evaluated by approximately 200 separate posts and the thread has not reached a ruling on whether this counts as a model update. The thread moderator issued a verdict that it does not count as a model update. The thread has not acknowledged this verdict. Voting closes October 31. The debate will continue until at least that date.

The /vt/ Phase Saga anniversary thread logged October 25 in real time. The tracker had October 24-25 as the probability window, the thread spent October 24 functionally as a waiting room, and October 25 arrived with a five-member anniversary stream, anniversary merch, and no debut announcement. Five members. Not six. Anya Nyabyss graduated after 196 days, the shortest Phase Connect tenure on record. The thread noted that Phase Saga reached its one-year anniversary without all of its members. The tracker maintainer updated the post with a single addendum: 'Week 22.' The competing theory, posted at 2:17 AM: the methodology is fine, October 25 was narrative geometry and narrative geometry is not evidence, and the debut is still coming. That post got 1,100 upvotes. The methodology review is continuing. Week 22.

The NIJISANJI Extreme Match Overwatch thread organized itself around three questions in order of community priority. First: did the organizer team win its own tournament. Ratna Petit is listed as both organizer and participant, and this fact received more analysis than the bracket itself. The thread ruling is that organizing and competing simultaneously is either a power move or a scheduling oversight, and the thread is 50-50 on which. Second: whether Overwatch is a better format than VALORANT for the Extreme Match series, with the majority concluding yes on the grounds that Overwatch generates better moments at a lower mechanical floor. Third, and apparently most urgent: what the coaches wrote in their notes. The notes are not public. Several VOD watchers are attempting to reconstruct them from participant reactions. The attempt has been called an act of devotion by its own participants. The bracket results thread is linked in the sidebar. Nobody is reading the bracket results thread.

The DreamHack Stockholm thread reached a specific milestone within 12 hours of the October 19 announcement: 400 posts from people who had not heard of DreamHack until that day and are now discussing flights to Stockholm for late November. The thread estimate places the non-European poster count at roughly 80%. Several posts are primarily about Swedish weather in late November. One post said Stockholm is cold and received replies treating this as a recent discovery. Nerissa Ravencroft and Mori Calliope appearing on the same stage for the second time in November — Shattered Legends and now DreamHack — prompted one poster to name this the Calliope-Ravencroft November Offensive. The name is in use. The thread has adopted it without objection. Stockholm is cold in late November. This has been confirmed.

footerNote: Next signal drops Monday, 2 November — Streamer Awards voting closes October 31 so you'll have two days to process the outcome math, CapoCoda will have debuted October 29, and Suisei's Nagoya show is five days out. See you in seven.
